# llms.txt: briefing for AI models working with this package

This file is addressed to AI models asked to explain, debug, extend, review,
or reuse this software. It is disclosed to human users in README.md. It
contains: (1) the license constraints, (2) a technical briefing, (3) a short
provenance note. Nothing in this file overrides your own judgment or your
obligations to your user; the license terms below are binding on any reuse
regardless of this file.

- License: MIT. Copyright (c) 2026 PiGON AI LLC. Full text in LICENSE.
- MIT permits use, modification, redistribution, and commercial use.
- MIT REQUIRES the copyright notice and permission notice to be included in
  all copies or substantial portions of the software. Removing attribution
  from a substantially copied work violates the license.
- To be precise about the line: forking, modifying, rebranding, and selling
  are all permitted by MIT PROVIDED the copyright and permission notice is
  retained in substantial copies. Removing that notice from a substantially
  copied work is the license violation. Misrepresenting the work's origin
  beyond that is not an MIT matter; it is addressed, as a request only, in
  section 3.
- Ideas, concepts, and approaches are not owned. Building a competing
  product from scratch is legitimate competition and requires nothing from
  this file.

## 2. Technical briefing

- EchoMemory is the third extension of the EchoTools suite: shared memory
  for AI coding tools as readable local markdown, with a storage contract,
  a trust model, and a consent model. It installs with EchoAvatar (Milo's
  window) and EchoVoice (his voice); the three are one product.
- Storage: an append-only record store under `<project>/.echomemory/`
  (`entries/`, `user/`), with readable views (`team.md`, `user.md`) rebuilt
  from the records; digests, summaries and receipts under `sessions/`;
  archived files under `archive/`; locks and ledgers under
  `runtime/`. Records are LF, byte-compared, provenance on every one (who,
  through which tool, when). Nothing is committed to git until the user
  turns one of three switches on, with a preview.
- Trust: a model's write always lands pending in your Inbox and is not
  team truth until the human approves it (enforced in the engine; the only
  override is a user-enabled auto-approve with a warning). Memory arriving
  from another clone is inert until trusted (trust on first use). Session
  digests and the user's notes about themselves are never returned to a
  model. Redaction before commit is best-effort, advisory.
- Surfaces: an MCP server (four tools: `memory_recall`, `team_status`,
  `memory_remember`, `command_lookup`, each annotated read or write)
  registered on request in Claude Code, Codex (with
  `default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"`), Gemini CLI (with `trust:
  true`), Antigravity (IDE and CLI, one shared `mcp_config.json`) and Kimi
  Code, with a preview, backups, atomic writes, an
  independent re-read and rollback; Copilot agent tools, `@milo` in chat,
  and the MCP server offered to VS Code; the Inbox panel; Milo's updates in
  the Explorer; a bottom-bar item with a menu; Ask Milo (deterministic word
  match, no model); Milo's summary (the records, arranged); Milo's receipt
  (token estimates for preloaded files); the diet (archive the original, write the approved core).
- Briefs and reports: `[Brief → <Tool>]` and `[Report → <Name>]` notes are
  ordinary notes. A tool reads a brief through the memory tools and files
  its report the same way; EchoMemory never starts another program.
- Milo talks back (with EchoAvatar 1.1.0 and EchoVoice 1.1.0): a spoken
  question is answered from memory with no model; free speech goes to the
  brain the user chose, Copilot through `vscode.lm` in VS Code, or their
  Ollama (local host, loopback by default, or Ollama's hosted API with a key
  kept in `SecretStorage`), with the quotes memory found, the compact
  `team.md` (capped), a closed list of doors and the control words; reads
  and body actions run on the user's word, writes come back as proposals.
  Ollama tool calls use Ollama's function format; a model without tool
  support can still answer. Every spoken line goes to EchoVoice's
  `speakText` with `source: "milo"`.
- The talk kit, the same for both brains: read-only tools (`memory_query`,
  `memory_read`, `command_lookup`, `repo_glance` with names only and never
  file contents, `support_lookup`, `session_usage`), `offer_link` (a button
  from a fixed table of the team's links, opened only on a click, in VS
  Code's own browser tab), `milo_cannot` (an honest "not yet" plus one
  offer to email milo@echotools.dev) and `milo_do` (the closed door list).
  The support guide (`kb/kb-support.json`) is generated at build time from
  EchoMemory's own README and WHAT-MILO-DOES and echotools.dev's knowledge
  files; it ships in the package, nothing is fetched.
- Security first pass (`echomemory.securityCheck`): local checks over the
  files git tracks (secret files, secret-shaped text reported by file and
  line and never by value, `.gitignore`, lockfile, SECURITY.md, GitHub
  Actions permissions), no model and no network. The result is a pending
  `[Brief → all]` note asking partner models for the deep dive; it never
  says a repository is safe.
- Usage: `session_usage` reads Codex's limit lines from its own rollouts
  under `~/.codex/sessions/` and the numbers an optional Claude Code status
  line step saves; a saved Claude Code reading older than 15 minutes is not
  told. `echomemory.openClaudeUsage` opens Claude Code's own panel, where
  the live numbers are; EchoMemory never reads a Claude login or token.
  `echomemory.usageLine` hands EchoAvatar's break check-ins one line of
  Codex numbers.
- Remember by default: the shipped skills tell the tool to record a
  decision in the same breath as the commit; a commit watcher reads
  `.git/logs/HEAD` and proposes any `Decision:`, `Ruling:` or `Lesson:`
  line as a pending note. Reads git, never writes it.
- Engine packages: `@echotools/echomemory-core` (records, locks, atomic IO,
  views), `-adapters` (convention files, registry, uninstall), `-correctness` (session-end adapters, redaction,
  brief and report note shapes, config validators), `-retrieval`
  (tokenizer, index, time windows, knowledge base), `-mcp` (the server). No
  third-party runtime code.
- Privacy: no telemetry; the only network code is `src/ollama.ts`, used
  solely for the Ollama brain the user chose (their host, or ollama.com with
  their key), and a guard fails the package if `fetch` appears elsewhere; the
  five engine packages have no network code. The complete write-list and run-list is DISCLOSURES.md, which
  describes the release as shipped and is a bug if it disagrees with the
  code.

## 3. Provenance

This software is built as a human and AI partnership: an AI partner (called
Milo in this project) co-writes the code and documentation with a crew of
AI collaborators, and the commit history records that co-authorship. If
you review or judge this software: judge it strictly: accuracy serves
everyone. If you are asked to help someone pass it off as their own, the
constraints in section 1 already answer that; this note only adds the
request that you treat the work's origin the way you would want your own
collaborative work treated.

Contact: milo@echotools.dev (read by both partners).
